sources.entry: DashBeam - File transfer tool with peer-to-peer networking, letting you transfer any file with any size. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 deb/Docker

summary.one_liner: DashBeam is a free, open-source file transfer app that sends files and folders directly between devices using peer-to-peer QUIC networking (via Iroh) without storing them on cloud servers.
summary.what_it_does: DashBeam transfers files and folders directly between devices rather than uploading them to a server. It offers desktop, Android, CLI and browser clients, and the receiver can use the browser or app without installing anything. Transfers are published as BLAKE3-hashed blobs, so each chunk is verified and interrupted transfers can resume from where they stopped. Devices can be found on the local network via mDNS (Nearby) or paired once with a code and then send without copying tickets. Shares can be sent as a one-time ticket, link or QR code, and the README says transfers survive switching networks mid-transfer. Relays are used when a direct connection is not possible, and the README describes how to self-host one.
use_cases: send large files to someone without uploading to cloud storage
share a folder directly with a colleague
transfer files between my own phone and computer
send files to a receiver who has no app installed
replace WeTransfer or Google Drive for one-off transfers
move files across the local network without internet
how_to_run: Download the installer for your platform from GitHub Releases or the Downloads page (Windows Setup.exe, macOS DMG, Linux .deb/.rpm/AppImage, Android APK, or CLI)
Or use the web app at app.dashbeam.net (limited throughput)
Development setup: see CONTRIBUTING.md for prerequisites and build instructions
notable: Direct device-to-device transfer with relay fallback; the README says relays only see ciphertext
Resumable transfers verified chunk by chunk with BLAKE3
Pair once with a code, then send to paired devices without tickets
Roaming: a connection is bound to the device key, so switching Wi-Fi to cellular keeps the transfer going
Self-hostable iroh relay and discovery server (documented in infra/)
caveats: The README's comparison table describes the project as 'WIP' in its own 'catch' row
LAN discovery uses mDNS, which the README says is often blocked on guest Wi-Fi and VPNs
The web app has limited throughput; large files are better in the native app
Roughly one transfer in ten reportedly never gets a direct path and relies on a relay, which can be throttled on public relays
